Background

Earlier this year a company announced they had “resurrected” dire wolves by gene editing gray wolf embryos (Servick 2025).

Colossal Biosciences, the company that led the dire wolf project, has asked you, a summer intern, to help analyze some of their data. It turns out they actually have produced a lot more wolves than they shared with the public (this is the made up part of the exam!).

1

Dire wolves were larger than today’s gray wolves. The average male gray wolf weighs 31 kg. Data below on 26 adult dire wolves the company has produced is available using

male_dire_weight <- read.csv("male_dire_weight.csv", stringsAsFactors = T)

Analyze the data to compare weights of dire and gray wolves. Make sure you include

  • null hypothesis (1 point)

  • alternative hypothesis (1 point)

  • explanation for test you will use (1.5 point)

  • results from statistical test (1 point)

  • clear explanation of how results relate to your stated hypotheses (1.5 point)

2

A few years later, the company has produced three “lines” of dire wolves using different gene editing techniques. Is there any evidence the three lines differ in weight? Data is available using

male_dire_weight_groups <- read.csv("male_dire_weight_groups.csv", stringsAsFactors = T)

Analyze the data. Make sure you include

  • null hypothesis (1 point)

  • alternative hypothesis (1 point)

  • explanation for test you will use (1.5 point)

  • results from statistical test (1 point)

  • clear explanation of how results relate to your stated hypotheses (1.5 point)

3

Dire wolves are also supposed to have smaller snouts relative to their body length than regular wolves. The company provided data from 25 of their dire wolves and 26 of the gray wolves that were used to source embryos. Is there evidence the dire wolves are different than gray wolves in regards to this relationship? Data is available using

snout_body_data <- read.csv("snout_body_data.csv", stringsAsFactors = T)

Make sure you include

  • null hypothesis (1 point)

  • alternative hypothesis (1 point)

  • explanation for test you will use (1.5 point)

  • results from statistical test (1 point)

  • clear explanation of how results relate to your stated hypotheses. Make sure to specify what your results say about the snout length - body length relationship(1.5 point)

Plot the data from question 3

5

The company also wants to know if the proportion of dire wolves born with white fur (a hallmark of dire wolves) is different than that of the gray wolves that provided the embryos (ignore any genetic issues here!). 18% of the parent gray wolves were white. For the litter in question, 18 out of 25 wolves were white. How would statistically analyze this?

How would you analyze the data. Make sure you include

  • null hypothesis (1 point)

  • alternative hypothesis (1 point)

  • explanation for test you will use (1.5 point)

  • results from statistical test (1 point)

  • clear explanation of how results relate to your stated hypotheses (1.5 point)
